LESSON: SIGN READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING- COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell the meaning of words and phrases in a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the main ideas in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. describe characters, ideas, or events in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. summarise information from a short text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. appreciate the importance of reading comprehension in lifelong learning. ● In groups, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or signed video clip related to the theme. ● In pairs, learners are guided to isolate, fingerspell and articulate sign vocabulary related traditional fashion. ● In groups, learners are guided to use digital devices to download and share texts with mental images from the texts and draw conclusions. ● In pairs, learners are guided to sign read a passage individually, and identify keywords in the passage. ● In pairs, learners are guided to infer the meaning of words using contextual clues. ● In groups, learners are guided to choose descriptive parts of the passage on traditional fashion and share the vivid images created in their mind. ● In pairs, learners are guided to describe characters, ideas, or events in a text. ● In groups, learners are guided to role- play the characters and events in the text. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading- Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking: Learner develops open mindedness and creativity as learners visualise characters, events, and places.

● Imagination: Learner makes observations as they gain new perspectives as they use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words.

Values:
● Responsibility: is reinforced as learners help each other to role-play characters, events and answer questions.

Link to other Subjects

The learner is able to relate the skill of intensive sign reading to their learning in all other subjects such as Creative Arts and Sports.
